text:
The memory covers several speakers across fifty-five sessions. Sessions 1 through 4 took place on Saturday, May 20, 2023. Sessions 5 through 12 took place on Sunday, May 21. Sessions 13 through 16 took place on Monday, May 22. Sessions 17 through 19 took place on Tuesday, May 23. Sessions 20 through 26 took place on Wednesday, May 24. Sessions 27 through 31 took place on Thursday, May 25. Sessions 32 and 33 took place on Friday, May 26. Sessions 34 through 39 took place on Saturday, May 27. Sessions 40 through 44 took place on Sunday, May 28. Sessions 45 through 49 took place on Monday, May 29. Sessions 50 through 55 took place on Tuesday, May 30. The user in sessions 1 through 44 never named their home city, employer, office, or neighborhood, so all local recommendations given to them are general and unverified.

For the morning routine, the earlier user works downtown and wants a quick, affordable grab-and-go coffee. The assistant suggested The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, Peet's Coffee, 7-Eleven, and Blue Bottle Coffee without confirming any is near the office. No chosen shop, usual order, or route is recorded. The user wakes at 6:30 AM on weekdays and planned 35 minutes for getting ready and eating. The assistant suggested padding this to 45 to 50 minutes and leaving between 7:45 and 8:00 AM. In session 30, a sister gave the user an espresso machine, which they are learning to use. In session 28, the user chose walnuts and chia seeds to add to their daily oatmeal with banana and honey, then decided to keep the honey. Whether this breakfast has started is not recorded. The user liked the Espresso Granola Parfait and Cappuccino Crepes, and the assistant suggested medium to medium-dark espresso roasts with unverified flavor notes. No coffee purchase is recorded. The user made a large batch of homemade granola, and the assistant advised airtight storage and freezing for up to six months, noting that granola is best within two to three weeks. The user is especially excited about tiramisu and also asked for an espresso brownie recipe. For lunch, the user packed a quinoa salad that they said was a hit. Eight mixed-greens salad suggestions were offered, and none has been chosen.

At home, the user grows basil, mint, cherry tomatoes, and peppers. In session 17, the assistant offered fifteen basil and mint recipe ideas and listed companion plants for cherry tomatoes, along with plants to avoid near them, including fennel, kohlrabi, potatoes, and rue. The user has harvested cherry tomatoes. The pepper plants have aphids, and neem oil did not work. The assistant listed insecticidal soap, horticultural oil, fine-mesh screens, aphid-resistant varieties, and longer-term ladybug and lacewing releases. No purchase or release is recorded. In session 30, the user decluttered the kitchen countertops and replaced an old toaster with a toaster oven they find very useful. In session 19, the user said they had replaced the bathroom light fixture about three weeks earlier. They reorganized their cabinets around May 20 or 21 and liked the zone idea, but no bin purchase is recorded. The user has used a Neutrogena cleanser and an Olay moisturizer for about two weeks and is happy with them. They plan to try the Neutrogena Hydro Boost Water Gel and the Olay Regenerist Micro-Sculpting Serum. The assistant's product claims are unverified, and it recommended patch testing and a dermatologist for concerns. The user likes Bath & Body Works candles.

For transportation, the user recently moved to a city about 10 miles from their previous home and has been taking a 35-minute bus. In session 3, they asked about a commuter bike. The assistant suggested finding shops through Google Maps, Yelp, or The League of American Bicyclists' Bike Shop Finder, test riding several bikes, and getting a fitting. The user was especially interested in a good lock and reflective gear. The assistant recommended busy, well-lit parking, a U-lock or chain rather than a cable, and locking both frame and wheels. It described the National Bike Registry and BikeIndex, said it knows of no registration program in the user's city, and suggested Google Maps, MapMyRide, or Ride with GPS for routes. The bike, lock, route, and registration choices are not recorded.

For health, in session 4 the user said they had been having digestive issues. The assistant offered general tips on whole foods, hydration, exercise, stress management, and prebiotic and probiotic foods, and advised seeing a healthcare provider if symptoms persist. No symptoms, history, medications, or diagnosis were discussed. The user has done Zumba for a few months, notices better cardio, and prefers fast Latin rhythms. They also take Pilates twice a week for flexibility and core strength, hoping it will help their tennis serves and volleys. In session 11, the user recalled a Wednesday yoga class at 7:30 PM, which the assistant could not confirm. A Latin pop and reggaeton playlist was planned, and it may not have been made. The user uses a fitness app and has an upcoming personal training session earned through it, with no date recorded. The assistant explained how to vet trainers by checking ACE, NASM, or NSCA certifications. In session 13, the user said they had played tennis five times in the past month on hard courts with their friend Alex and wants a new court. The assistant suggested search methods, the local Parks and Recreation department, and private clubs. The user struggles with consistency, footwork, and positioning. The assistant suggested a continental or eastern grip, slice and toss drills for the backhand, the split step, the carioca drill, and filming oneself. It advised demoing racquets, noting that a new racquet helps mainly if the current one is outdated or mismatched. No racquet purchase is recorded.

For travel, the user is planning a Tokyo trip. In session 7, they said they are staying at a hotel near the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku and asked for traditional restaurants. The assistant listed six with walking times and suggested booking through Chope, TableCheck, or the hotel concierge, all unverified. The user said they exchanged money on February 1, when the rate was favorable, and now have ¥50,000. The foreign amount and exact rate are not recorded. The assistant gave general airport transfer options for Narita and Haneda and suggested a Suica or Pasmo card. The user then said they booked a round-trip ticket "three months ago on December 15th" and hope to see cherry blossoms. The assistant said cherry blossom season usually runs from late March to early April, so February is typically too early, and suggested winter illuminations and hot pot. December 15 is about five months before May 21, not three, so the booking date conflicts with the user's own statement. Travel dates, airport, and hotel have never been confirmed. Separately, the user said they would love to visit Nepal one day.

For language, the user wants to learn Mandarin, expecting it to differ greatly from the Romance languages they know. In session 14, the assistant listed online courses, exchange platforms such as HelloTalk, italki, Tandem, and Verbling, textbooks, and podcasts, none checked. The user also asked about European and Brazilian Portuguese because a Brazilian colleague uses idioms they do not understand, and the assistant gave simplified, unverified differences. The user often code-switches between English and Spanish with bilingual friends. The user is considering a local language school offering Mandarin, Arabic, and Korean, but the school was never named and no enrollment is recorded.

For work, the user serves on a Board of Trustees. In session 12, they asked how the board can evaluate its collaboration with external stakeholders, and the assistant suggested surveys, evaluation meetings, metrics, and reports. The user plans a stakeholder survey and follow-up interviews, but the organization and timeline are not named. In session 15, the user asked whether anchoring or reverse anchoring is better for pricing, and the assistant said anchoring suits premium services while reverse anchoring suits growing volume. In session 21, the user said they are building a startup and asked about social media advertising and SEO. The assistant covered audience definition, platform choice, retargeting, small budgets, keyword tools, and tracking. The user attended a four-day entrepreneurship conference in November 2022, where they pitched to investors, and plans a blog post and a LinkedIn share. The startup's name, product, and stage are not recorded, and the post's publication status is unknown. In session 29, the user described a web application for trading used books, where buyers queue for a book and sellers choose which buyer to trade with. The assistant produced ten functional requirements and a fourteen-point UI/UX plan. Whether this is a personal project, startup, or course assignment is not recorded.

For coding, the user is building a Python backend with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic, apparently involving user accounts. In session 31, the user asked about increasing a database connection pool size. The assistant first gave a `databases` example with `pool_size`. The user said they use `create_async_engine` and got "TypeError: Invalid argument(s) 'pool_size' sent to create_engine()." The assistant then said `create_async_engine` does not accept `pool_size` and suggested a `create_asyncpg_pool` function and a `PooledDatabase` class with `max_size`. These APIs are unreliable, and the general claim that `create_async_engine` never accepts `pool_size` is inaccurate. The issue remains unresolved. The User model has id, email (unique and indexed), username (unique), full_name and bio, hashed_password, created_at, and updated_at. The assistant proposed a UserOut response model and a POST /signup endpoint, noting that hashed_password must never be returned. The UserSignInRequest and POST /signin example was flawed: it used `json_data` before defining it and relied on `dict()`, the Pydantic v1 method, where `model_dump()` is the v2 equivalent. The user's Pydantic version and final code are not recorded.

For loyalty programs, in session 32 the user said they were trying to maximize points across stores. They had just redeemed points at Safeway and were close to Gold status at Starbucks, which the user said requires 500 stars, and the assistant agreed. For Petco, the assistant advised joining Pals Rewards, watching for double-points days, and buying in bulk, with unverified point rates. For H&M Membership, the assistant described one point per dollar, rewards at 100 points for $5, and tiers at $200 and $500 annual spending, all possibly inaccurate. No sign-ups or purchases are recorded.

For entertainment, in session 22 the user said they had watched a romantic comedy called "Love in the Time of Pride" at the Outfest Los Angeles LGBTQ+ Film Festival. The assistant found no record of it, and the user insisted on the title, so its existence remains unverified. Ten rom-coms were recommended, and the user is especially interested in To All the Boys I've Loved Before and Love, Simon. In session 34, the user said they play board games often, including at a monthly game night. The assistant recommended ten games, and the user said Gloomhaven is their top pick and that they had pre-ordered Azul. For games to play with their sister, the assistant suggested Mysterium, Deception: Murder in Hong Kong, and Codenames, and the user plans to try Mysterium with her. In session 40, the user said they have been on a board game kick for about two months, usually playing with three to five people. They have played Codenames, Pandemic, and Azul, and want to try Scythe and Mysterium. They asked about Spirit Island, which the assistant described as a cooperative game by R. Eric Reuss for one to four players. In session 39, the user said they were thinking of buying noise-blocking headphones for concerts and had just returned from a Billie Eilish concert at the Los Angeles Forum with their best friend, Rachel. The assistant recommended headphone types and listed LA venues, with unverified claims. The user plans to attend a classical concert with the LA Philharmonic at the Hollywood Bowl. No concert has been booked and no headphones bought. In session 38, the user said they had been experimenting with cocktails, including a Spicy Mango Margarita. The assistant's unique bitters may not exist. In session 37, the user asked the assistant to write a literature review on EPSS acceptance among instructional designers, using a 22-item bibliography. Several citations are mismatched or unverified, and the review was not checked. In session 41, the user said they are new to model building, with a 1/48 F-16C finished and a 1/35 T-34 tank and a 1/24 Ford Mustang GT500 in progress. Oil washes for rust did not look right. The assistant's "Russian Rust" set of Mig paints and its four named colors are unverified and possibly invented. In session 42, the user collects vinyl and traded duplicates for a "rare 1962 Miles Davis album," "Miles Davis: Blue Moods." The assistant's date, label, and personnel for that album are unverified and conflict with known releases. Some of its claims about John Coltrane's albums are doubtful. In session 43, the user asked how Methodist leaders are responding to the LGBTQ+ inclusion controversy. The assistant named Bishop Karen Oliveto and Bishop Scott Jones, and wrongly described the Global Methodist Church as fully accepting LGBTQ+ individuals, when it is a traditionalist body. No personal religious affiliation is recorded. In session 44, the user asked the assistant to create a persona named Julie, a fictional married stay-at-home mom with two young kids. Julie's traits describe the persona, not the user, unless the user says otherwise.

Earlier sessions covered several general topics. Session 5 addressed virtual reality in education, with the view that VR is more likely to enhance than replace traditional teaching. Session 6 addressed how a financial institution could raise profitability and reduce delinquency, with five personas requested. Session 9 described anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress among World War I soldiers, with some unchecked historical details. Session 10 produced an essay on Kevin Barry's Night Boat to Tangier, shorter than requested. Session 18 had no user question, but the assistant produced a false "live update" claiming Argentina led France 2-0 in the World Cup Final. The assistant has no live access, and the 2022 final ended 3-3 before Argentina won on penalties. Session 19 began with a request for a reliable plumber, but no plumber has been named. Session 20 asked about researchers on small mammals and tree replanting in Western Canada, with unverified names. Session 23 asked about Pari traditional foods and dress, but the Pari tribe could not be verified. Session 25 covered a family dinner for the user's mom's 60th birthday. The user said their mom has been dealing with health issues and chose a lemon blueberry poppy seed cake with a Blueberry Lemon Glaze, with general, untested amounts. The user is considering fresh flowers, but no florist or purchase is recorded, and the party date, guest count, and venue are unknown. Session 26 covered The Big Short and Wall Street greed, and the user plans to volunteer at an unnamed local nonprofit. Session 27 produced headings for a study on whole blood clot wound care, keeping the user's spelling "Venus," possibly a typo for "Venous." Session 33 covered Afghanistan, with unverified cost figures. Session 36 asked for a profit analysis of C(x)=8x+10 and R(x)=-4x^2+88x, but the assistant's reply is blank. From the stated functions, profit is P(x)=-4x^2+80x-10, peaking at 10 leashes, with maximum profit of $390 at $48 per leash. These figures are derived by this memory, not taken from the assistant's reply.

Sessions 45 through 48 took place on May 29 and appear to involve a different person, since their content does not match the earlier user's profile. In session 45, a user said they are a refugee who was just granted asylum in the US, left family and friends in Syria in July, and is still adjusting. English is not their first language. They asked how to apply for a social security number. The assistant listed documents, including an asylum approval letter or Form I-589, a passport, an I-94 if available, and proof of age, then described Form SS-5, an SSA office visit, and a card mailed within two to four weeks. The phone numbers, the ORAO email, and the timeline are unverified. It suggested SSA multilingual services, refugee resettlement agencies such as IRC and USCRI, and interpreter lines, with unverified details. It then described a state ID application through the DMV and mentioned REAL ID without verified details. For a bank account, it described an asylum document and passport as primary identification, with a social security card or state ID as secondary, and advised calling ahead about asylee requirements. None of these steps is recorded as completed. In session 46, a test message asked for something interesting, and the assistant claimed chess has about 10^120 possible games, compared with about 10^80 atoms in the observable universe. In session 47, a user planned a $25 to $30 gift for a neighbor who has been helping with yard work. The user chose wine, and the assistant listed five wines with unverified prices, plus a short handwritten note. No purchase is recorded. In session 48, a user asked how a trustee handles conflicts of interest with beneficiaries. The assistant said the trustee must disclose conflicts and seek informed consent, may need to resign if conflicts cannot be resolved, and should consult professionals. It listed six fiduciary duties: loyalty, prudence, impartiality, communication, record-keeping, and compliance. The user's purpose is not recorded, and it may or may not connect to the earlier Board of Trustees work.

Session 49, on May 29 at 21:10, involves a user who asked for a level 8 D&D one-shot with stat blocks, loot, a final battle with a surprise twist, lair actions, and detailed traps. The assistant's reply, "The Lost Temple of the Djinn," centers on Zoltar, a once-just Djinn whose temple was lost to the sands, and a wealthy collector who hires the party to retrieve an artifact. Its enemies are four mummies, two construct guardians, and six skeletal warriors. The stat blocks contain errors: "Psychicical" is a typo, "Monster Manuel" should be Monster Manual, and several traits are not verified rules. The visible text ends mid-trap, so the loot, twist, lair actions, final battle, and remaining traps are not shown.

Session 50, on May 30 at 02:36, involves a developer whose test reports are XML files formatted with XSL and driven by JavaScript and ActiveX. The reports are viewed in Internet Explorer or through the IETab plugin in Chrome. The ActiveX accesses the file system so that when a developer clicks an Accept button, the test references in tcml files, which are XML in fact, are modified. The user wants the reports to run in Chrome without a plugin or disabled security features, and wants to keep the XML references under source control. The assistant gave steps including converting XML to JSON, replacing XSL with Handlebars or Mustache, replacing ActiveX with a server-side web service with authentication, and testing across browsers. The user considered keeping tcml references as XML and storing XML chunks inside JSON fields. The assistant's Handlebars example implied raw XML chunks would render as markup, which is inaccurate, since Handlebars escapes output by default. Whether the user adopted any approach is not recorded.

Session 51, on May 30 at 06:12, involves a premium men's undershirt brand with a machine learning model's list of concepts and index scores. The assistant removed several concepts at the user's direction, including buying shares, maternity, tug, shirts and tank tops, polyester, and hate the feeling. The revised list has errors: polyester clothing appears twice, and women, boys, and jeans remain despite being off-brand. The assistant then wrote short consumer narratives, including unverified claims about RibbedTee and Tencel, but the text cuts off at "feel hot."

Session 52, on May 30 at 06:24, involves a user working on social housing in Ireland. Its first assistant message, with no user question shown, is a ten-point outline for a statement titled "Government's Decision to Lift Eviction Ban Threatens Thousands of Families Amid Economic Uncertainty." The claim that the government lifted the eviction ban is unverified. The user then asked for ideas to motivate Irish voters, and the assistant gave ten, including celebrity partnerships, town halls, and school programs. A later fundraising request produced ten strategies, including grants and EU programs such as the ERDF, ESF, and EIB, which are unverified for Ireland. Finally, the user asked for an email to persuade retired construction professionals to help acquire land and build units. The assistant drafted a template with placeholders and four requests: land evaluation, mentorship, project management, and advocacy. No organization, contact, or response is recorded.

Session 53, on May 30 at 11:23, involves a user who asked about threats to wild orangutans and what is being done about them. The assistant named habitat loss from agriculture, logging, mining, and settlement as the main threat, followed by poaching, climate change, and human-wildlife conflict. Its measures included protected areas, law enforcement, forest restoration, education, and sustainable livelihoods. It named the Orangutan Conservancy, the Borneo Orangutan Survival Foundation, and the Sumatran Orangutan Conservation Programme, which it said has worked since 1994. It cited Indonesia's 2011 moratorium on new logging permits in primary forests and peatlands, which is broadly consistent with known policy, and described the Kinabatangan Orangutan Conservation Project in Sabah, which is unverified. For results, it cited four studies on Tanjung Puting densities, Sabah reintroduction, Sumatran outreach, and Kerinci Seblat enforcement. All four are unverified and should not be relied on. It claimed Singapore promotes sustainable palm oil and Australia committed $6 million over four years in 2016, both unverified. It said the US Lacey Act restricts trade in illegally sourced wildlife, which is accurate. For individual action, it suggested raising awareness, reducing palm oil in processed foods, supporting the named organizations, buying sustainable products, and choosing responsible ecotourism. The user's location, purpose, and follow-up plans are not recorded.

Session 54, on May 30 at 14:26, involves a user who asked for an overview of Disney's content changes since it acquired Star Wars and Marvel. The assistant described the Star Wars sequel films, Clone Wars and Rebels, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which it said has over 20 movies, a figure likely outdated. It listed Darth Vader as a Disney-era villain, which is inaccurate since Vader predates the acquisition. In later turns, the user, who identifies as a long-time fan, said Disney ruined Star Wars, that the new films lack the magic of the original trilogy, that Disney prioritized profit, did not consult original creators, and rehashes storylines. The assistant repeatedly said it does not hold opinions, then discussed both sides. It noted that Mark Hamill, Harrison Ford, and Carrie Fisher returned, which is accurate, and claimed Disney hired new writers and directors in response to criticism, which is vague and unverified. The user's views are opinions they stated, and the assistant did not endorse them.

Session 55, on May 30 at 17:46, involves a user who asked how Columbia University supports student entrepreneurship. The assistant named the Columbia Startup Lab, the Columbia Entrepreneurship Program, Columbia Technology Ventures, Columbia Business School's entrepreneurship center, and funds including the Columbia Venture Competition, "Seed Capital Funding," and the Lang Fund for Entrepreneurship. These are unchecked, and "Seed Capital Funding" is doubtful. Asked about successful startups, the assistant said Venmo was co-founded by two Columbia alumni, Andrew Kortina and Iqram Magdon-Ismail, and acquired by PayPal for $800 million in 2013, which is broadly consistent with known facts. It said Warby Parker had a Columbia graduate among its Wharton founders, which is wrong, and gave a valuation over $3 billion as unverified. It said Blue Apron earned $881 million in its 2017 IPO, which is likely wrong, and described Harry's, co-founded by Jeff Raider, as a Columbia Business School alumnus company, which is unverified since Raider is associated with Wharton. Asked about current startups to watch, the assistant named beagle learning, pilleve, smart vision labs, and tara, with unverified features. These companies could not be confirmed and may be invented. The user's affiliation and purpose are not recorded.

Several items remain open for the earlier user. No coffee shop, bike, lock, racquet, tennis court, personal trainer, language school, plumber, or Mig paint has been chosen. Ladybug or lacewing releases, bin purchases, skincare trials, and the Zumba playlist are unconfirmed. Their city, office, home, and startup locations remain unknown. The Tokyo dates, airport, hotel, restaurants, and exchange amount are unconfirmed, and the December 15 booking conflicts with "three months ago." The mom's party details and flowers are unknown. The breakfast, espresso drinks, granola, tiramisu, and brownies are plans, not confirmed routines. The pool-size problem and the de/serialization example remain unresolved. The startup's stage, blog publication, Board survey timeline, pricing project, and web app status are unknown. The board game collection, Gloomhaven purchase, Azul delivery, Scythe, Spirit Island, the sister game night, and the personal training date are unconfirmed. No headphones, concert tickets, or Hollywood Bowl booking have been recorded. The cocktails, literature review, Miles Davis album, and T-34 and Mustang progress have not been confirmed as made or used. The leash profit question went unanswered. For the asylee user in session 45, the SSN, state ID, and bank account steps are not recorded as completed, and no SSA appointment or DMV visit is confirmed. For the neighbor gift in session 47, no wine, basket, or card has been purchased. For the sessions 49 through 52 users, the D&D one-shot's remaining sections, the XML modernization approach, the undershirt list, and the Ireland statement and email have not been confirmed as used. For the session 53 orangutan user, no donation, volunteer work, or product change is recorded. For the session 55 user, no startup, program application, or meeting with any named Columbia program is recorded. No purchases, appointments, reservations, enrollments, or firm commitments are recorded beyond the plans users described.

This memory covers forty-two sessions across eleven days, from Saturday, May 20, 2023 through Tuesday, May 30, 2023. Sessions 1 through 4 are dated May 20, Sessions 5 through 7 May 21, Sessions 8 and 9 May 22, Sessions 10 through 19 May 23, Sessions 20 through 24 May 24, Session 25 May 25, Sessions 26 through 28 May 26, Sessions 29 through 31 May 27, Sessions 32 through 36 May 28, Sessions 37 and 38 May 29, and Sessions 39 through 42 May 30. The user is the person I talk with, and the assistant is the earlier version of me. Words like "yesterday" are relative to each session's header date. Details the assistant gave that it could not verify are flagged below and should be treated as guesses, not facts.

The user is a Data Scientist at a San Francisco startup and a former financial analyst with two years at a mid-sized Chicago firm, though a Chicago location also came up in May without explanation. They hold a master's degree, recently received graduation congratulations, and have a thesis advisor, Dr. Smith, whose lab they are considering. On May 30 they said they are moving to Los Angeles for a UCLA master's program before classes start, and that they had been stressing about the application three months earlier but now it is coming together. How the UCLA program relates to the earlier master's and the San Francisco job is not recorded. They are building financial modeling and business skills and are interested in AI in healthcare and education. They are most productive from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m., usually lunch at 12:30, and use Todoist. They live with an abuela who speaks Spanish, practice with her daily, and are beginning French. They own a brown Fjallraven bag, a dog named Max, a cat named Luna, a Canon EOS R6, and a 50mm f/1.8 lens. Their interests include indie folk, African diaspora culture, Korean-inspired cooking, antiques, acting, sports, and travel, and they play midfield in Sunday soccer at a community center. They have shown interest in Surinamese and Romanian (Wallachian) culture, though no personal connection to either is recorded.

On May 20 at 2:42 a.m., the user planned to attend an unnamed music festival with no dates or tickets confirmed and asked how to keep belongings safe. The assistant suggested a zippered valuables pouch, a strapped phone, contact information on the bag, separated ID and cards, a portable charger, an agreed meeting spot, and secure storage. The user lost the bag tag and used a business card instead; whether a replacement was bought is unknown. The user said they are most interested in cross-functional skills, especially business acumen. The assistant's Certified Financial Modeler details are unverified, and no enrollment has been reported. The user scheduled a 9:00 a.m. creative project meeting and chose Todoist. The claim that Todoist syncs with Google Calendar is unconfirmed.

On May 21, the user said they practice Spanish daily with their abuela, who moved in about three months earlier, and that this has improved their fluency. The assistant recommended Duolingo, Babbel, and Anki, with descriptions that may be inaccurate, and overstated Anki's effect on cognitive load, which the evidence does not support. No French level, schedule, or app has been confirmed. The assistant also wrote an exhibition text titled "The Plastic Wasteland," centered on the user's handmade rug that alters the IKEA logo to read "MERDA." Its claim of "50 contemporary artists and 50 conceptual artists" and its artist lists are unreliable, including deceased artists such as Eduardo Paolozzi, Mark Rothko, and Marcel Duchamp. The exhibition, rug, and location are unconfirmed. The assistant recommended *The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo*, *The Nightingale*, *The Silent Patient*, *The Farm*, *The Undocumented Americans*, and *Say Nothing*, and the user was interested in all of them. The user is active in a Facebook group called Book Lovers Unite and tracks reading on Goodreads, though neither membership nor shelves are fully confirmed.

On May 22 at 6:49 a.m., the user pasted copy for the #Endgame cryptocurrency project, listed at dapp.endgame.black, for rewriting. The source describes treasury wallets, validator rebalancing to fund buybacks, and a seven-year referral program. Its "Airdrop Raffles" section never mentions raffles, yet the assistant's rewrites added raffle language. The tax section sets a 20 percent sell tax, reduced by 10 points through referrals, though the wording is ambiguous. The assistant invented a flat fee, a large-transaction fee, a referral fee, and the claim that the "Dynamic Whale Tax" encourages larger trades. Nothing confirms that the copy is published or that the dApp, airdrops, or tax structure are live. In Session 9, the user was interested in indie folk. The assistant suggested S. Carey, Beirut, The Head and the Heart, and Lord Huron, then listed Chicago venues, festivals, and record stores, all unverified. These included the Chicago Folk Festival (June 11 to 13) and Lollapalooza (July 29 to August 1), which is not primarily a folk festival. A February 22 show by The Head and the Heart has already passed, and the assistant wrongly described Chicago Music Exchange as online-only.

On May 23, at 4:53 a.m., the user planned a family reunion next summer, timed with their nephew's high school graduation, with a backyard BBQ and a slideshow of his childhood and high school years. The nephew's name, the date, the location, and the guest count are unknown. The user wants a mix of instrumental and sentimental songs, but none has been picked. The assistant's suggestions for editing tools, composers, and quotes attributed to public figures are unverified. At 6:51 a.m., the user asked personal questions about a rescheduled team meeting, their usual yoga day, a Tuesday dentist appointment, flossing, and which day they overslept. None of these details is recorded, and the assistant wrongly said it had no way to know such things. A future assistant should answer from memory when relevant and say plainly when a detail is missing. The assistant also recommended Wunderlist, which was discontinued and folded into Microsoft To Do, so it should not be recommended as current. The user weighed a summer trip to Europe on Lufthansa or Norwegian Air. Lufthansa seemed good at $850 return from New York to Frankfurt. The New York departure conflicts with the Chicago and San Francisco locations mentioned elsewhere, and its reason is unknown. Nothing is booked, and no travel dates are set. The user also mentioned an American Airlines email about a possible AAdvantage class action, whose contents the assistant does not know. Twice the user asked whether the assistant had airline membership or baggage knowledge. It has neither, and baggage rules change, so the user should check the airline's site. The user also asked about a company called Spector. The assistant had no current information, and the user's connection to Spector is not recorded.

Also on May 23, the user asked how Stripe judges transactions legitimate. The assistant's checks and fraud tools were not verified against current documentation. When asked about storing transaction data, it wrongly said PCI DSS requires storing the security code. In fact, PCI DSS prohibits storing sensitive authentication data, including the CVV, after authorization. Only the account number, name, and expiration date may be stored, and only in protected form when needed. The user asked for reminders for Max and Luna. The assistant repeatedly said it had added items to a "virtual sticky note" and would set reminders. It cannot do either, so no reminders exist. Luna's grain-free wet food needs reordering around May 27 or 28, since about a week remains and delivery takes two to three days. Max needs a monthly flea and tick preventive, probably last applied around late April, but the date and product are unknown. Vet dates, Luna's medication, and the supplement check are unrecorded. They value honesty about what is known and dislike being assumed to know more than they do. They get frustrated by generalities when they ask for specifics, so give concrete, checkable facts or say clearly that you lack them.

For the aquarium thread they like short numbered references and the standing command "list plants." For professional threads they expect structured documents. For the report and schedule they want time blocks and priorities. For technical threads they want copy-ready commands and step-by-step troubleshooting. For marketing they want concrete steps. For personal budgeting they want categorised running totals. For writing tasks they want exact word counts. For trip planning they want costs checked against budgets. For fitness they like practical tips and specific product choices. For collecting they want realistic price ranges and warnings about authenticity.

They enjoy humour, logic puzzles, EDM and high-energy music, and free verse poetry. Keep replies direct and avoid overstating certainty. Be especially careful with health, therapy, medical imaging, legal, and factual history or science topics.
